The validation and "include all teams with 0" fixes are fine, but the tie-break change is wrong relative to the docstring, even though it makes the test suite pass.

The docstring says: "When two or more teams share the highest quotient, the desk goes to the one with the larger headcount." The new key uses `-headcounts[team]` as the secondary sort criterion for `max()`, which actually selects the team with the *smaller* headcount on a tie (negating reverses the ordering), not the larger one.

I verified this actually matters for `test_quarterly_floor_plan` (`platform: 60, design: 30, support: 16`, 6 desks):
- Round 2: quotients tie at 30 for platform (60/2) and design (30/1). Per the docstring, platform (larger headcount) should win. But if platform wins here, tracing the rest of the D'Hondt rounds yields `{platform: 4, design: 1, support: 1}`, not the `{platform: 3, design: 2, support: 1}` the test expects.
- The test only passes if design (the smaller headcount) wins that tie and the analogous tie again at round 6 — i.e. exactly the opposite of what the docstring specifies.

I confirmed the other tests with distinct headcounts (`test_proportional_split`, `test_larger_floor`) never hit an exact quotient tie between different headcounts, so they don't exercise this rule either way — only `test_quarterly_floor_plan` does, and it requires the reverse of the documented behavior.

So this PR makes the suite green by encoding "smaller headcount wins ties" into the algorithm, which contradicts the explicit docstring contract the teammate asked to be treated as the source of truth. The PR description also claims this "correctly implements" the documented tie-breaking rule, which isn't accurate.

This needs to be resolved by reconciling the conflict — either the docstring is stale and needs correcting (call that out explicitly, since the teammate should decide), or the sign should be flipped back to match the docstring and `test_quarterly_floor_plan` needs to be revisited with the teammate (not silently patched to fit). Please don't merge as-is; the implementation silently contradicts its own documented spec.
